_metadata.scope: General action semantics and parameterized recipes for the ten AtomMotor actions; no dataset rows or target structures.

change_atom_action.summary: Replace the species at one zero-based site index; retain its position and properties.
pitfalls: replace_species changes ALL sites of a species; use replace(index, ...).
change_atom_action.code:
structure = input_structure.copy()
site = structure[index]
structure.replace(index, species, properties=site.properties, label=site.label)

remove_atom_action.summary: Remove exactly the requested site. The remaining sites retain their relative order.
pitfalls: For multiple removals, calculate indices before mutation and call remove_sites once.

add_atom_action.summary: Append one atom at the specified absolute Cartesian position in angstrom.
add_atom_action.parameters: species: element symbol; position: length-3 Cartesian vector
pitfalls: Set coords_are_cartesian=True; do not interpret this vector as fractional coordinates or as a displacement.
add_atom_action.code:
structure = input_structure.copy()
structure.append(species, position, coords_are_cartesian=True, validate_proximity=False)

move_atom_action.summary: Translate one atom by a Cartesian displacement in angstrom.
move_atom_action.parameters: index: int; displacement: length-3 Cartesian vector
pitfalls: The vector is added to the original position, not assigned as the new position.
Do not wrap the result into the cell during the requested edit.
move_atom_action.code:
structure = input_structure.copy()
structure.translate_sites([index], displacement, frac_coords=False, to_unit_cell=False)

move_towards_atom_action.summary: Move the first atom by distance angstrom along the direct Cartesian vector toward the second atom.
move_towards_atom_action.parameters: index1, index2: int; distance: float in angstrom
pitfalls: Normalize r2-r1; distance is a length, not a fractional ratio.
The pinned action uses the direct vector, not a minimum-image vector; the second atom stays fixed.
move_towards_atom_action.code:
import numpy as np
structure = input_structure.copy()
direction = structure[index2].coords - structure[index1].coords
length = np.linalg.norm(direction)
if length == 0:
    raise ValueError("The two sites have coincident Cartesian positions")
structure.translate_sites([index1], distance * direction / length,
                          frac_coords=False, to_unit_cell=False)

insert_between_atoms_action.summary: Append an atom on the direct line from the first site toward the second, distance angstrom from the first.
insert_between_atoms_action.parameters: index1, index2: int; species: element symbol; distance: float in angstrom
pitfalls: Use r1 + distance * (r2-r1)/norm(r2-r1), not the midpoint unless specified.
Do not apply minimum-image geometry. The upstream generator rounds the displayed distance to two decimals; the hidden ratio is unavailable.
insert_between_atoms_action.code:
import numpy as np
structure = input_structure.copy()
start = structure[index1].coords.copy()
direction = structure[index2].coords - start
length = np.linalg.norm(direction)
if length == 0:
    raise ValueError("Cannot define a line between coincident sites")
position = start + distance * direction / length
structure.append(species, position, coords_are_cartesian=True, validate_proximity=False)

swap_atoms_action.summary: Exchange the two species at their fixed sites, preserving all Cartesian positions.
pitfalls: The pinned implementation swaps species even though its prompt says swap spatial positions. For CIF geometry these give the same species-position multiset; site identity differs.
Capture both original species before either replacement.
swap_atoms_action.code:
structure = input_structure.copy()
first, second = structure[index1], structure[index2]
structure.replace(index1, second.species, properties=first.properties, label=first.label)
structure.replace(index2, first.species, properties=second.properties, label=second.label)

delete_below_atom_action.summary: Delete sites with Cartesian z strictly below the reference site; retain equal-height sites.
pitfalls: Snapshot z before deleting. Fractional z is not Cartesian height in a tilted cell.
Pinned-source discrepancy: execute uses strict z < z_ref and never adds the reference site, even when the generated text says Including itself. This recipe follows that implementation.
delete_below_atom_action.code:
structure = input_structure.copy()
z = structure.cart_coords[:, 2].copy()
indices = [i for i, value in enumerate(z) if value < z[index]]
if not indices:
    raise ValueError("No sites below the reference site")
structure.remove_sites(indices)

rotate_around_atom_action.summary: Select original neighbors by periodic shortest distance < radius, excluding the center; rotate their stored Cartesian coordinates around the center.
rotate_around_atom_action.parameters: index: int; radius: angstrom; angle: degrees; axis: nonzero Cartesian vector
pitfalls: Right-hand rotation; radians are required by pymatgen rotate_sites.
Use MIC only for neighbor selection. Pinned AtomWorld rotates original coordinates, not their nearest periodic images; keep the lattice fixed.
rotate_around_atom_action.code:
import numpy as np
structure = input_structure.copy()
center = structure[index].coords.copy()
selected = [i for i in range(len(structure))
            if i != index and structure.get_distance(index, i) < radius]
if np.linalg.norm(axis) == 0:
    raise ValueError("Rotation axis must be nonzero")
if selected:
    structure.rotate_sites(selected, theta=np.deg2rad(angle), axis=axis,
                           anchor=center, to_unit_cell=False)

super_cell_action.summary: Repeat the existing unit cell along each lattice vector by positive integer factors.
super_cell_action.parameters: repeats: three positive integers (na, nb, nc)
pitfalls: Atom count and volume multiply by na*nb*nc. Scaling only the lattice strains the material and is not a supercell.
pymatgen and ASE use different output site ordering; their species-position multisets agree for structure evaluation.
super_cell_action.code:
import numpy as np
structure = input_structure.copy()
if len(repeats) != 3 or any(int(n) != n or n <= 0 for n in repeats):
    raise ValueError("Expected three positive integer repeats")
structure.make_supercell([int(n) for n in repeats], to_unit_cell=False)
